History of the DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court was established in 1839 as a county-level court in Illinois. Over time, the court evolved into a Circuit Court system, gaining additional jurisdiction and authority. Today, the DuPage County Circuit Court is one of the largest and busiest trial courts in the state, handling tens of thousands of cases each year.

Structure of the DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court is divided into two main divisions: the Civil Division and the Criminal Division. Each division has its own presiding judge, who oversees the daily operations and functions of the court.

The Civil Division handles civil disputes, such as contract disputes, personal injury cases, and family law matters. The Criminal Division handles criminal cases, including felony and misdemeanor cases, traffic offenses, and juvenile cases. The DuPage County Circuit Court also has a Probate Division, which handles estate matters, guardianship cases, and mental health cases.

Functions of the DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court performs several essential functions, including resolving disputes, interpreting the law, and administering justice. The court also handles various administrative tasks, such as collecting and distributing fines and fees, processing court documents and records, and managing court operations.

Types of Cases Handled by the DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court handles a wide range of cases, including civil disputes, criminal cases, and family law matters. Some of the common case types handled by the court include:

  • Personal injury cases
  • Contract disputes
  • Property disputes
  • Divorce and family law matters
  • Criminal cases, including felony and misdemeanor charges
  • Traffic offenses
  • Juvenile cases

Accessing Court Records and Documents

The DuPage County Circuit Court maintains a comprehensive record of court proceedings, which includes court filings, court orders, and transcripts of hearings and trials. Members of the public can access these court records and documents by visiting the courthouse in person or by accessing them online through the court's website.

Services Offered by the DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court provides several essential services to the public, including:

  • Self-help services for litigants without attorneys
  • Courtroom interpretation services for non-English speakers
  • Alternative dispute resolution services, such as mediation and arbitration
  • Jury services
  • E-filing and online payment services

DuPage County Circuit Court Judges

The DuPage County Circuit Court has over 30 judges who preside over civil, criminal, and probate cases. Judges are appointed by the Illinois Supreme Court and serve six-year terms. Each judge has their own courtroom and caseload, and they are responsible for overseeing all aspects of the cases that come before them.

Alternative Dispute Resolution Services

The DuPage County Circuit Court offers several alternative dispute resolution (ADR) services, including mediation and arbitration. These services allow parties to resolve disputes outside of court, which can save time and money. ADR services are available in civil cases, family law matters, and some criminal cases.

The Jury System in DuPage County Circuit Court

The DuPage County Circuit Court has an active jury system, which allows citizens to participate in the justice system by serving as jurors. Jurors are selected randomly from a pool of registered voters and are required to serve for a specified period of time. Jury duty is an essential civic duty that helps ensure the fairness and impartiality of the justice system.

Courtroom Etiquette and Procedures

If you have a legal matter that requires you to appear in court, it is important to understand courtroom etiquette and procedures. This includes dress code, behavior expectations, and rules for presenting evidence and arguments. The DuPage County Circuit Court provides information and resources to help litigants understand what to expect when appearing in court.

Filing Fees and Payment Options

The DuPage County Circuit Court charges fees for filing court documents and for certain court services, such as requesting copies of court records. Filing fees can vary depending on the type of case and the specific service being requested. The court accepts various forms of payment, including credit cards, cash, and checks.

Pro Se Litigants in DuPage County Circuit Court

Pro se litigants are individuals who represent themselves in court without the assistance of an attorney. The DuPage County Circuit Court provides self-help services for pro se litigants, including access to legal resources and guidance on court procedures. However, it is important to note that representing yourself in court can be challenging and may not be the best course of action in all cases.

Appeals and Appellate Court in DuPage County

If you are unhappy with the outcome of your case in DuPage County Circuit Court, you may have the option to file an appeal. Appeals are heard by the Illinois Appellate Court, which is located in DuPage County. The Appellate Court reviews the trial court's decision for errors and can overturn or modify the decision if necessary.

If you are looking for a specific case in DuPage County, you can also search for it by name using the DuPage County Court Case Search by Name tool. This tool allows you to search for cases by the last name of the plaintiff, defendant, or attorney.

C. 18th Judicial Circuit Case Search

The 18th Judicial Circuit Case Search is a statewide case search tool that allows you to search for cases in DuPage County as well as other counties in Illinois. This tool provides access to case information, including court dates, case summaries, and court orders.

D. Circuit Court Case Lookup

The Circuit Court Case Lookup is another online tool that allows you to search for cases in the DuPage County Circuit Court. This tool provides access to case information, including court dates, case summaries, and court orders.

E. DuPage County E-access

DuPage County Eaccess is a subscription-based service that provides access to court records and case information. This service is available to attorneys, government agencies, and the general public. DuPage County Eaccess provides access to case information, court orders, and other court documents.

DuPage County Divorce Records

If you are looking for divorce records in DuPage County, you can request them from the DuPage County Circuit Court Clerk's Office. Divorce records are considered public records and can be accessed by anyone. You can request divorce records in person or by mail.

Conclusion

The DuPage County Circuit Court is an essential component of the justice system in Illinois. Whether you are a litigant in a legal matter or a member of the public seeking information or services, understanding how the court works and what services it provides is crucial. By following the guidelines and procedures set forth by the DuPage County Circuit Court, you can ensure that your legal matter is handled fairly and efficiently.
